Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- Test setup and scenario:
  - The failing test constructs an encoding Base64InputStream with lineLength=0 and lineSeparator=null, then calls read() five times:
    - Base64InputStream in = new Base64InputStream(new Codec105ErrorInputStream(), true, 0, null);
    - for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++) { in.read(); }
  - In encoding mode, Base64InputStream.read() delegates to read(byte[], 0, 1), repeatedly requesting a single output byte.

- Critical code paths:
  - Base64InputStream.read():
    - Calls read(singleByte, 0, 1) and returns the single byte value or -1.
  - Base64InputStream.read(byte[], int, int):
    - When the internal Base64 buffer is empty (!base64.hasData()), it reads a chunk from the underlying stream into a fresh temporary buf (size 4096 when encoding).
    - If c > 0 and the caller’s output array exactly matches the requested length (b.length == len), it unconditionally forwards that array to Base64 via base64.setInitialBuffer(b, offset, len).
    - Then, since doEncode is true, it calls base64.encode(buf, 0, c) to fill the Base64 internal buffer with encoded data.
  - Base64.setInitialBuffer(byte[], int, int):
    - Replaces Base64’s internal buffer pointer with the caller-provided array b and sets pos/readPos to the given offset.
  - Base64.encode(byte[], int, int):
    - Writes encoded output in 4-byte blocks. Before writing, it does a single capacity check:
      - if (buffer == null || buffer.length - pos < encodeSize) resizeBuffer();
    - Then it writes 4 bytes (and possibly line separators if lineLength > 0).

- Why the bug happens (ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException after many read() calls):
  - In this usage pattern, each Base64InputStream.read() call supplies an output array of length 1 (the field "singleByte").
  - The code Base64InputStream.read(byte[], int, int) unconditionally forwards this 1-byte array to Base64 via setInitialBuffer when c > 0 and b.length == len. In encoding mode, this is unsafe:
    - Encoding produces output in 4-byte chunks; a 1-byte buffer cannot hold even a single chunk.
    - Base64.encode() does check capacity and calls resizeBuffer(), but encode() only performs one such check per iteration, relying on resizeBuffer() to ensure sufficient space for encodeSize bytes.
    - Starting from a 1-byte buffer, an implementation of resizeBuffer() that grows incrementally (e.g., doubles size without ensuring buffer.length - pos >= encodeSize) can leave the buffer still too small (e.g., 2 bytes), after which encode() immediately writes 4 bytes, causing ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException (index 2).
  - This is consistent with the stack trace pointing to Base64.encode and the test’s repeated single-byte reads: after the internal buffer is drained (readResults sets buffer = null), the next iteration reassigns Base64’s internal buffer back to the 1-byte singleByte array, triggering the unsafe situation again. The failure after many successful reads (e.g., 10920) reflects that it occurs upon a particular boundary when a new encode cycle starts from that 1-byte initial buffer.

- Key faulty interaction:
  - Base64InputStream.read(byte[], int, int) uses base64.setInitialBuffer(b, offset, len) for any c > 0 and b.length == len, regardless of doEncode.
  - That optimization is valid for decoding (where the output fits into the caller’s provided buffer) but is unsafe for encoding, where the encoded output exceeds the caller’s requested single byte.

- Conclusion:
  - The ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException is caused by Base64InputStream passing the caller’s tiny output buffer (length 1) as Base64’s internal buffer in encoding mode. Base64.encode then attempts to write 4-byte blocks into that buffer; even with a resize attempt, a single capacity check combined with incremental resizing can leave the buffer too small, leading to out-of-bounds writes.
  - The correct behavior is to avoid setInitialBuffer when encoding (or to ensure that setInitialBuffer is only used when the provided buffer is guaranteed to have sufficient capacity for the immediate encoding output).

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).

Base64InputStream.read(byte[], int, int)
Base64.setInitialBuffer(byte[], int, int)
